source_text: Tempus admonet ut ad alia transeamus; sed in eodem loco restare aliquid indignatione compellor. Tune audeas dicere Adam voluntate peccasse? Unde tibi venit hoc somnium? Quia iniquum, inquis, erat, ut imputaret in peccatum Deus, nisi a quo abstinere liberum nosset. Quid ergo? Hanc iustitiam ille princeps tenebrarum quem colitis, ad momentum ei crediderat, et eam propediem reposcens hunc Deum omni aequitate destituit, ut qui intellexerat a primordio non esse imputandum in peccatum, nisi unde liberum fuerat abstinere, per omne reliquum tempus a cunctis nascentibus noverit abstinere liberum non fuisse? Postremo, unde tu nosti illud tantummodo iustum fuisse, ut in Adam nisi voluntarium crimen non possit ulcisci; si iniustum esse non nosti, imputari cuiquam in crimen, quod fatearis sine voluntate susceptum? Aut ergo opinionem traducis iustam putabis, ut Dei possit convenire sententiae, cum imputat peccatum parvulo, quod sit nulla eius voluntate commissum, et cogeris illud quoque iustum et Dei conveniens iudiciis profiteri, ut Adae imputaverit in peccatum, quod noverat ab eo non voluntate, sed substantiae suae deformitate prolatum; perque hoc ipsum nulla erit tradux, nec depravata operantis arbitrio, sed male instituta ab exordio natura reprehendetur, confiteberisque te esse Manichaeum. Aut si resipiscens iniustum esse dixeris, ut Adam teneretur reus pro naturae suae culpis; irrefutabiliter consequitur, scelestissimum esse, si Abel, Enoch, Noe et omne hominum genus obnoxium crimini originali censeatur. Quod facinus iudicii si admoveas Deo tuo, solus pro omnibus remanebit reus; apparebitque, quod semper, non ipsum esse, quem catholici aequissimum in Trinitate veneramur. Quod si a Dei accusatione destiteris, Manichaeae traducis, qua hactenus confossus es, vel redivivus dogma damnabis.
pass_a_gloss: Time warns that we pass to other things; but I am compelled by indignation that something remains in the same place. Do you dare to say Adam sinned by will? From where did this dream come to you? Because it was unjust, you say, that God would impute into sin except that from which he knew it was free to abstain. What therefore? Had that prince of darkness whom you worship believed this justice to him for a moment, and soon demanding it back did he strip this God of all equity, so that he who had understood from the beginning that it must not be imputed into sin except that from which it had been free to abstain, through all remaining time knew it had not been free to abstain from all being born? Finally, from where do you know that that only was just, that in Adam a charge cannot be avenged except voluntary; if you do not know it is unjust that it be imputed to anyone into a charge, which you confess was taken up without will? Either therefore you will think the opinion of the tradux just, so that it can suit God's sentence, when he imputes to a little one a sin which was committed by no will of his, and you are compelled to profess that that also just and suiting God's judgments, that he imputed into sin to Adam what he knew was brought forth by him not by will but by a deformity of his substance; and through this itself there will be no tradux, nor a nature depraved by the decision of the one working, but badly instituted from the beginning will be blamed, and you will confess you are a Manichaean. Or if coming to your senses you shall have said it is unjust that Adam would be held guilty for the faults of his nature; it irrefutably follows that it is most wicked if Abel, Enoch, Noah and the whole genus of humans is judged liable to an original charge. Which crime of judgment if you apply to your God, he alone for all will remain guilty; and it will appear, as always, that he is not him whom the catholics venerate as most equitable in the Trinity. But if you shall have desisted from an accusation of God, you will, even revived, condemn the dogma of the Manichaean tradux, by which you have thus far been pierced.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
Blaise originalis; Julian's mali originalis, not a later system slogan
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: Time urges us to move on, but indignation forces me to linger here a little. Do you dare say Adam sinned voluntarily? Where did this dream come from? ‘Because,’ you say, ‘it would have been unjust for God to count something as sin unless he knew the person was free to abstain.’ What then? Did the prince of darkness whom you worship lend him this justice for a moment, then soon demand it back and strip this god of all fairness? At the beginning he understood that nothing should be counted as sin except what could freely be avoided; afterward, through all remaining time, he knew that every newborn lacked freedom to abstain.

Finally, how do you know that the only just course in Adam’s case was to punish voluntary guilt, unless you know it unjust to charge anyone with a crime admittedly received without will? Either you will consider inherited sin just, so that it can fit God’s judgment when he charges an infant with a sin committed without any will of the infant. Then you will be forced to profess it equally just and fitting for God’s judgments to have charged Adam with a sin he knew arose not from Adam’s will but from the deformity of his substance. In that case there will be no transmission of sin: the nature condemned will not have been corrupted by its agent’s choice, but badly established from the beginning, and you will confess yourself a Manichaean.

Or, coming to your senses, you will say it would be unjust to hold Adam guilty for his nature’s faults. Then it follows irrefutably that it would be utterly wicked to judge Abel, Enoch, Noah, and the whole human race liable for original guilt. If you attach this crime of judgment to your god, he alone will remain guilty in place of everyone. It will appear, as always, that he is not the God whom we catholics worship as perfectly just in the Trinity. But if you stop accusing God, you will condemn the doctrine of Manichaean inherited sin that has pierced you until now, as though returning to life.

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian names the opinion of original evil (mali originalis) as what Rom 5:12's 'one man' crushed; keep his phrase, not a later original-sin system.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
